paper_metadata.title: Improving Credit Card Transaction Fraud Detection Using CVQBoosting

experiments.description: Hybrid CVQBoost fraud-detection experiment on the MLG-ULB Kaggle credit card fraud dataset using KNN weak classifiers and the Dirac-3 photonic processor to optimize ensemble weights.

algorithm.variant: CVQBoost on Dirac-3 with KNN weak classifiers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Weak-classifier selection and weighting were formulated as an energy minimization problem and sent to the Dirac-3 processor; the paper does not specify a qubit-to-variable mapping.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize ensemble energy to select and weight weak classifiers for fraud detection.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Not specified beyond the CVQBoost Hamiltonian/energy-minimization formulation.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Hamiltonian constructed from the weak-classifier ensemble and sent to Dirac-3.

problem_instance.description: Credit card fraud detection on the MLG-ULB Kaggle benchmark with severe class imbalance.
problem_instance.dataset_name: MLG-ULB Kaggle Credit Card Fraud Detection

dataset_specification.description: Rows with missing values were removed; labels mapped to ±1; features scaled to [0, 1]; dataset split 70/30 into training and test folds; training fold oversampled with SMOTE; test fold kept original; repeated over 10 independent runs with different random seeds and random splits.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Remove missing rows, map labels to ±1, scale features to [0, 1], 70/30 train-test split, SMOTE on training fold only, repeated resampling of fixed test fold with validation/evaluation split for threshold calibration.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Average over 10 independent runs with different random seeds; metrics reported include precision, recall, accuracy, AUC-ROC, and AUC-PR.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Weak classifiers were built classically on an AMD Ryzen 5 5600G CPU; Hamiltonian was constructed classically before submission to Dirac-3; data cleaning, scaling, SMOTE, and train/test splitting were performed classically.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Dirac-3 returned weights for weak classifiers, which were then used by a classical model for inference; repeated resampling and threshold calibration were performed classically.
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: Typically less than 10 seconds for relaxation schedule 2, according to the discussion.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports a performance improvement in AUC-PR over a classical baseline, but no runtime speedup claim for the full CVQBoost-KNN pipeline; the KNN weak-classifier construction is actually the slowest among the tested weak learners.
